Where Heritage Meets Cloud Comfort

Some stories aren’t written. They are stitched.

Before Beads & Bloom becomes something you wear, it begins with hands that remember—generational master karigars rooted in Punjab, working with patience, precision, and cultural pride. For decades, wearing traditional ethnic footwear meant enduring painful shoe bites, stiff cardboard soles, and blisters after just an hour on the dance floor.

We set out to change this without losing the soul of the craft. We paired centuries-old dabka, zardozi, and authentic sheesha mirror work with modern orthopedic footbed engineering—giving every woman the freedom to celebrate India’s most joyous weddings, sangeets, and galas in pure, uncompromised comfort.

"We don't modernise by westernising. We refine what already belongs to us."

Frequently Asked Sizing Questions

Direct answers to help you choose the ideal size for maximum handcrafted comfort.

Q.How do I measure my foot size for Beads & Bloom juttis?

Place a measuring tape flat on the floor against a wall. Measure your foot length from the heel to the tip of your longest toe in centimeters. Compare this measurement with our EU size guide (sizes 36 to 41).

Q.What size should I choose if I have broad feet?

If you have broad feet or fall between two sizes, we recommend sizing up by one size for optimal comfort and fit.

Q.Do handcrafted Punjabi juttis stretch over time?

Yes. Authentic handcrafted juttis with genuine leather or textile bases mold gently to the contours of your feet with wear, enhancing overall comfort over time.

Q.Can I exchange my juttis if the size does not fit?

Yes, we accept exchanges for size within 48 hours of delivery, provided the juttis are unworn, in original packaging, and accompanied by a continuous unboxing video.

Artisanal Footwear Preservation

Handcrafted Jutti Care Guide

Every pair of Beads & Bloom footwear is handcrafted by skilled Punjabi artisans. Follow these simple steps to preserve delicate embroidery and buttery-soft leather soles for years.

1. Moisture & Water Defense

Our juttis are constructed with 100% genuine leather soles and linings. Genuine leather breathes naturally and conforms to your feet, but prolonged exposure to moisture can cause stiffening or water stains.

  • Never submerge, wash, or clean juttis under running water.
  • Avoid wearing delicate embroidered pairs outdoors in active rain or wet grass.
  • If wet, pat dry with a soft cloth and let them dry naturally away from artificial heat.
Leather Protection Tip

2. Cleaning by Fabric & Craft

Different materials require tailored cleaning techniques to protect intricate hand-embroidery, dabka, and mirror work:

  • Velvet & Suede: Gently brush with a dry, soft toothbrush or velvet sponge in the direction of the nap to remove surface dust.
  • Pure Silk & Crepe: Wipe very lightly with a clean, slightly damp muslin cloth; never rub aggressively.
  • Zardozi, Cut-dana & Mirrors: Lightly dust with a soft makeup brush to remove dust from between metallic crevices without snagging threads.
Embroidery Preservation

3. Storage & Humidity Control

Proper seasonal storage prevents metallic zari tarnishing and preserves the silhouette of your juttis:

  • Always store juttis in breathable cotton or muslin bags—never airtight plastic bags.
  • Place silica gel sachets inside your shoe box during humid monsoon months.
  • Stuff toe boxes loosely with acid-free butter paper to maintain their curved silhouette when not in use.
Long-Term Storage

4. Breaking-In & Bite Prevention

All Beads & Bloom juttis feature signature double-cushioned memory foam footbeds. Here is how to achieve the absolute best comfort:

  • Genuine leather stretches gently across the width after the first wear, contouring to your unique foot shape.
  • For wedding ceremonies, wear your juttis for 20 minutes at home before the main event.
  • Apply a tiny dab of mustard oil or petroleum jelly along inner seams if you have exceptionally sensitive skin.
Signature Comfort

Common Questions

Frequently Asked Care Questions

Clear answers to help you maintain artisanal quality and all-day comfort.

Q.Can I wash my handcrafted Punjabi juttis with water?

No. Never wash your juttis with water or submerge them. Beads & Bloom juttis feature 100% genuine leather soles and linings, which absorb water and may lose structural integrity or stain delicate embroidery when soaked. Always dry clean or spot clean gently with a dry, soft-bristled brush.

Q.What should I do if my juttis accidentally get wet in the rain?

If exposed to dampness or rain, immediately pat dry with a clean cotton towel. Allow them to air-dry naturally at room temperature in a well-ventilated space. Never use hair dryers, heaters, or leave them under direct harsh sunlight, as intense heat hardens and cracks genuine leather.

Q.How do I prevent metallic zardozi and dabka embroidery from tarnishing?

Always put your juttis on AFTER applying perfume, deodorants, hairspray, and foot lotions. Chemical sprays cause metallic zari, cut-dana, and dabka threads to oxidize and tarnish over time. Store each pair in a breathable muslin cloth bag with silica gel packets to keep moisture away.

Q.How do I break in new juttis to ensure bite-free wear for weddings?

While Beads & Bloom juttis feature signature double-cushioned memory foam footbeds to eliminate shoe bites, authentic leather naturally conforms to your foot contours over time. We recommend wearing your new pair with thin cotton socks around the house for 20–30 minutes a couple of days before your big wedding or festive celebration.

The Indian Bride's Footwear Guide

Bridal Jutti Buying & Styling Guide

From the mandap to the sangeet stage, Indian wedding celebrations demand hours on your feet. Discover how handcrafted Punjabi juttis deliver royal bridal elegance with 10-hour bite-free comfort.

Comfort Meets Tradition

Why Modern Brides Choose Juttis Over High Heels

A traditional bridal lehenga can easily weigh between 15 and 25 kilograms with its layered cancan, heavy dupatta, and dense zardozi embellishments. Standing on hard marble mandaps or walking across garden lawns in 4-inch stilettos places acute pressure on your lower back and knees.

Handcrafted Punjabi juttis ground your stride naturally. With genuine flat leather soles, soft leather linings, and signature double-cushioned memory foam footbeds, Beads & Bloom juttis ensure you walk down the aisle with poise, grace, and complete physical comfort.

No Lawn Sinking
Double Memory Foam
100% Genuine Leather Soles

The Pheras Test

During Hindu Pheras or the Sikh Anand Karaj, rituals require removing shoes or walking around the sacred fire repeatedly. Handcrafted juttis slip on and off effortlessly, making transitional ceremonies smooth and stress-free.

Tailor Alteration Tip:

Always take your wedding juttis to your lehenga trial. The height of flat footwear changes the hem drop by 3–4 inches compared to heels. Hemming to flats prevents tripping on your skirt.

Haldi and Mehendi celebrations require joyful colors and easy mobility. Opt for lightweight raw silk or satin juttis featuring mirrors, gotta patti, or lively floral threadwork that complement yellow, lime green, and fuchsia lehengas or shararas.

Bridal Footwear Answers

Frequently Asked Bridal Questions

Should I wear juttis or high heels for my wedding ceremony?

Most Indian brides now choose handcrafted juttis or keep a pair as their primary footwear for ceremonies. Heavy bridal lehengas (weighing 15–25 kg) combined with 4–6 hours of standing during the Anand Karaj or Pheras can cause severe foot fatigue in high heels. Handcrafted juttis with genuine leather soles and double-padded memory foam cushioning offer heirloom elegance without back or foot strain.

When should I order my bridal juttis relative to my lehenga fittings?

We recommend purchasing your bridal juttis at least 3 to 4 weeks before your final lehenga alteration. Take your wedding juttis to your lehenga trial so your master tailor can hem the skirt length accurately to grazing height, preventing any tripping hazard while walking down the aisle.

How do I match jutti embroidery with my bridal outfit?

Look at your outfit's primary metallic embellishments. If your lehenga features warm antique zardozi, choose juttis with dabka and antique gold cord work. If your lehenga highlights pearls, mirrors, or silver tilla work, opt for ivory or pearl-embellished pairs. For pastel outfits, matching or complementary tone-on-tone thread embroidery creates a cohesive royal look.

Can I get personalized bridal sizing and styling consultations?

Yes! Our bridal concierge provides one-on-one virtual styling and sizing guidance via WhatsApp and email. Share your lehenga swatch or wedding outfit details, and our bridal specialists will guide you on the ideal palette, embroidery match, and comfortable fit.

We collect personal information necessary to provide products, fulfill orders, and offer customer support. This may include:

  • Order and transaction history (items purchased, payment method selected).
  • Technical device information, IP address, and browser characteristics during site navigation.

2. Third-Party Service Providers

We share required data with verified third-party partners solely to operate our store and deliver your orders:

  • Payment Gateways: Razorpay handles secure online payment transactions. Card or banking credentials are not stored on our servers.
  • Logistics & Couriers: Shiprocket and authorized courier partners receive recipient names, addresses, and phone numbers to facilitate parcel delivery.
